messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — we saw a big 95th/99th pct latency spike on the eu-dedicated cluster between ~02:10-02:25 UTC. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.2s and overall throughput dropped ~30%.
apm-bot: [alert] high-p95-latency on /v1/generate (eu-dedicated). link: https://apm.redwood/alerts/2381 :rotating_light:
sunil: Do we have autoscaler logs? did nodes fail to come up or were they busy after provision?
oliver: Looking at runtime traces — many requests fell back to a slower kernel path during that window. Kernel selector kicked fallback for larger batches. Profiling gist below:

```
kernel_selector: selected_kernel="fast_int8_attn_v2" fallback="slow_attention"
reasons: batch_size=48 (>32 threshold), seq_len=1024
latency_contrib: attention_kernel +180ms per token
```

oliver: The selector heuristic uses a fixed batch threshold tied to model profile. We saw bursty batching (clients aggregated locally) that pushed many requests over that threshold and made the runtime choose the slower kernel.
jen: Also noticed a lot of cold-starts — several worker pods took 80-120s to become healthy due to KV cache priming + model warmup. That amplified latency while autoscaler was still provisioning.
maria.g: So two factors: (1) kernel selector fallback for large batches, (2) autoscaling + cold-start delays -> compounded effect.
danielle: Any noisy neighbor evidence? did GPU owners show contention or fragmentation?
oliver: Yes, one host had >95% GPU mem fragmentation and a stuck long-lived job. Snippet from node logs:

```
node-17.nyc | nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
2026-03-17 02:12:03 | 14997 MiB, 16384 MiB
2026-03-17 02:13:10 | 15240 MiB, 16384 MiB  <-- fragmentation + ephemeral spikes
```

oliver: That host's allocator failed to satisfy contiguous KV cache allocation quickly, so the pod init waited and delayed readiness.
sunil: Autoscaler metrics: provisioning_time p95=95s (should be ~30s). Warm pool had size=2 but we needed ~6 during that traffic pattern.

```
kubectl get hpa autoscaler-eu -o jsonpath='{.status.currentReplicas} {.status.desiredReplicas}'
=> 6 9

provisioning_events: 02:09:40 -> 02:11:50 (node ctrl plane scheduling delay)
```

maria.g: Quick mitigations:
- increase warm_pool_size eu-dedicated from 2 -> 6 (temporary)
- reduce scale cooldown from 120s -> 45s
- tweak kernel selector to prefer fast kernel up to batch 64 for this model (canary)
- drain noisy node-17 and reprovision

jen: I pushed a canary kernel-selector tweak to staging, committing hash 7f3b2a9. It biases toward fast path for batch <=64 and adds telemetry. Plan to canary on 1% first.

```
git rev-parse --short HEAD => 7f3b2a9
patch: runtime/kernel_selector: raise batch_threshold for model-x -> 64
```

deploy-bot: Started canary deploy runtime-v2.3.4-canary to eu-dedicated (1% traffic)

apm-bot: Canary perf: p95 reduced by ~120ms on canary slice. No errors observed in 15m smoke.
danielle: Follow-ups — we need long-term fixes:
- make kernel selection adaptive (online profiling: measure actual seq_len/batch histogram and pick kernel per-batch, not static threshold)
- improve KV cache allocation fallback to prefer partial allocation and async priming (avoid blocking readiness)
- add metrics for gpu-mem-fragmentation and expose allocator failures to alerting
- reevaluate warm_pool sizing algorithm to consider burstiness (percentile-based target)

sunil: Agreed. I'll open an RFC for adaptive selector + allocator improvements. I'll also add a small change to autoscaler to include a "fastpath" prewarm API (trigger immediate ephemeral prewarm when arrival rate > X).

maria.g: Immediate actions taken: warm_pool_size bumped, node-17 cordoned + drained, canary kernel tweak rolled to 1% and then 10% after positive signals. Autoscaler cooldown lowered.

oliver: Post-mortem notes from profiling:
- root cause chain: client-side bursty batching -> kernel selector threshold -> slow kernel -> increased per-request CPU/GPU time -> autoscaler triggered but provisioning lag + KV priming -> cold-starts delayed -> noisy neighbor (fragmentation) amplified allocation latency.
- regression: selector threshold had been tightened in commit 3a1c9b (Dec) to reduce memory overhead; that turned out brittle for bursty traffic.

jen: Will revert 3a1c9b and replace with adaptive approach in next sprint. Opening PRs:
- PR#4123: kernel-selector adaptive metric + telemetry
- PR#4124: KV allocator partial-alloc + async prime

danielle: I added SLO post-incident task: add warm-pool autosizing alert when observed p95 provisioning_time > 60s for 5m.

maria.g: Thanks all — running incident review tomorrow 09:30 PT. Assigning owners: sunil (autoscaler changes), oliver (kernel selector), jen (KV allocator), danielle (alerts + dashboards). Anything else?

sunil: Will also prototype pre-provisioning API and measure cost impact.

maria.g: Great. Closing thread here; will paste postmortem doc link after review.

maria.g: postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/2026-03-17-autoscale-coldstart-lag
